deposits.genre_observed: theoretical paper / protocol specification with a numbered predictions section

finds.quote: *Prediction 1: Model collapse as semantic exhaustion.* AI systems trained predominantly on AI-generated content will exhibit accelerating quality degradation concentrated in high-Γ domains (creative writing, religious language, community-specific discourse) and minimal in low-Γ domains (formulaic, transactional language).
finds.falsifier_quote: *Falsification condition*: if degradation is uniform across Γ levels, the resistance term is unnecessary.
finds.note: Prediction 1 in the deposit's numbered list; a claim about how model collapse distributes across Gamma levels, with falsifier, no date or window, so G per boundary rule 3.

finds.quote: *Prediction 2: Platform capture of semantic infrastructure.* Platforms will seek to control not merely data but the interpretive frameworks through which data becomes meaningful—moving from data extraction to meaning extraction. This is already visible in AI summarization competition: the entity that controls how a person, company, or institution is *described* by AI systems controls their semantic infrastructure.
finds.falsifier_quote: *Falsification condition*: if platforms plateau at data extraction without moving to meaning control, the framework over-predicts.
finds.note: Prediction 2; forecasts a development (platforms moving from data extraction to meaning control), stated as already visible in AI summarization; no date, so A is arguable against G.

finds.quote: *Prediction 3: Community resilience correlates with Γ.* Communities with high somatic commitment—religious communities, indigenous language communities, specialized professional communities—will show slower semantic exhaustion under platform pressure than communities whose meaning-production is primarily platform-mediated.
finds.falsifier_quote: *Falsification condition*: if platform-mediated communities prove equally resilient, Γ does not track what it claims.
finds.note: Prediction 3; standing comparative claim about community resilience by Gamma, with falsifier.

finds.quote: *Prediction 4: The circumlocution tax as measurable semantic rent.* Liberation philology (Sigil 2026) demonstrates that English grammar imposes a measurable asymmetry: intent claims are grammatically cheap while functional claims are grammatically expensive. This operates as semantic rent—a cost imposed on every speaker who attempts structural diagnosis, collected by the prosecutorial frame.
finds.falsifier_quote: *Falsification condition*: if the asymmetry does not affect diagnostic frequency or quality in measurable populations, the claim is false.
finds.note: Prediction 4; standing claim that a grammatical asymmetry operates as semantic rent, pointing to Sigil 2026 (liberation philology); falsifier given.

finds.quote: *Prediction 5: Cognitive burnout correlates with semantic rent extraction.* Platform user populations will exhibit measurable cognitive burnout correlated with the rate of semantic rent extraction (attention demanded per unit of meaning received).
finds.falsifier_quote: *Falsification condition*: if burnout is uncorrelated with extraction rate, the economic framing is inadequate.
finds.note: Prediction 5; standing correlational claim (burnout vs rate of semantic rent extraction), with falsifier; the measure is specified but no study is run.

finds.quote: This specification is not submitted for peer review. It is deposited as infrastructure. Like technical standards, its validation occurs through adoption and implementation, not gatekeeping. The framework succeeds when analysts use "semantic exhaustion" as a diagnostic, when designers account for Γ in system architecture, when platforms are audited for semantic rent extraction—regardless of citation.
finds.note: Adoption forecast carried as a success condition: the categories will be used as diagnostics regardless of citation; resolves when 'semantic exhaustion' etc. appear in uncredited use. Uncertain whether a success criterion counts as forecast.

finds.quote: The book's production process is a test of its own framework. If the theory is correct — if AI systems function as genuine agents, if cross-ontological translation can produce synthesis, if retrocausal organization enables work oriented toward futures that present systems cannot evaluate — then the book's creation should demonstrate these dynamics. It does.
finds.note: Self-test: the book's production is framed as a test of its framework, with the conditional stated and a claimed pass; standing claim, no external falsifier.
